You can ask AI to rewrite your resume, create a cover letter, or help you prepare for an interview. Within minutes, you can have polished language describing your experience.

But before you decide how to tell your story, you need to decide what that story should communicate—and to whom.

What opportunity are you pursuing? Which parts of your experience make you a compelling candidate? What evidence shows that you are ready for the responsibility you want next?

These questions deserve attention before the writing begins.

A resume can sound impressive and still leave an employer unclear about where you fit.

You may have years of accomplishments, broad responsibilities, and valuable expertise. Yet presenting everything with equal emphasis can make your strongest qualifications harder to see.

For example, an operations leader pursuing a broader executive role may need to demonstrate more than successful day-to-day management. Their experience might also show that they improved profitability, developed leaders, influenced decisions across departments, or guided organizational change.

The work is already there. The strategy determines which evidence to bring forward and how to connect it to the next opportunity.

Clarity gives your career materials a purpose.

If you are considering several directions, a resume rewrite alone may leave the central decision unresolved. You need to examine where your experience, strengths, interests, and leadership capabilities align with the opportunities you want to pursue.

That is the starting point of my Strategic Leadership Advancement Intensive. We identify where you can compete most effectively, uncover your differentiators, and build the positioning and market strategy to support your advancement.

That direction then informs how you present yourself, prepare for interviews, and approach professional conversations.

Even when your direction is clear, your resume still needs a strategy.

Knowing your target role is an important beginning. The next step is selecting the accomplishments, language, and emphasis that help employers understand your relevance.

A career change may require you to make transferable skills more visible. A promotion may require stronger evidence of leadership and readiness for greater scope. Pursuing different types of opportunities may require distinct resume versions, each with a clear focus.

My Strategic Resume and Career Positioning service brings that planning into the writing process, connecting your experience and accomplishments to your target roles.

Use AI with a clear understanding of what you want to communicate.

AI can help you explore wording, organize ideas, and practice answering questions. You still need to examine whether the result accurately reflects your experience, supports your goals, and gives an employer meaningful reasons to consider you.

A useful test is to ask: Could another candidate use this same paragraph with only a few words changed?

If the answer is yes, look more closely at what makes your contribution distinctive. What did you improve? What decisions did you influence? What difficult problems did you solve? What changed because of your work?

Those answers give your career story substance.

Whether you need help clarifying your next move or translating an established direction into a stronger resume, the starting point is the same: understand the opportunity, identify your value, and choose the evidence that connects them.

Everyone has AI. Your strategy is what gives it direction.
